source_unit_checks.clause_self_check: Each clause has a direct ruling supported by its selected operative quotes.

operative_quotes:
1. Each player takes an action card and all pieces of one player color. Put every scoring chip on **0**. Choose a banker; put money and tiles within reach.
2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.
5. Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.
answers.answer: Deal two cards to each player. Each claims the two initial lots and receives money equal to the two cards’ printed values during setup only; discard those cards in matching color/Strip spaces. Split remaining deck into four roughly equal stacks, put End of Game atop the fourth, then put the other three above it.

Each normal turn has **Draw**, then **Play**: draw a property card, acquire its lot or die, pay every marked lot, pay money and score points for the indicated casinos, discard the card in its appropriate pile, then take actions in Play. Trading is also possible at any time, subject to the restrictions below.
answers.answer: Highest roller starts; after every turn pass the player card left. Normal turn is Draw first (acquire, lot payout, casino payout/scoring, discard), then Play.

operative_quotes:
1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.
2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.
3. **The indicated casinos pay money and points:** a single-color card pays every casino of that color anywhere on the board. A **Pay The Strip** card instead pays every casino with at least **one edge adjacent to The Strip**, regardless of color. A qualifying casino pays for **all its tiles**, not only the tile touching The Strip.
4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.
5. Discard the property card in its appropriate color/Strip pile so the number already drawn remains countable. Proceed to Play, except that two-player F cards repeat Draw as described below.

operative_quotes: A **casino** is one tile or an edge-connected group of same-color tiles on the same block. Same-color edge neighbors merge immediately into one casino, even if their dice belong to different players. Diagonal contact alone does not connect them; casinos cannot be subdivided after joining.

The **boss** is the player owning the **highest individual die** in that casino, not the most dice or the highest sum of pips. Several highest dice belonging to the same player are sufficient to make that player boss. Resolve highest ties between different players immediately as described under **Boss ties**.
answers.answer: Edge-connected same-color tiles on the same block merge immediately; diagonal contact does not. Joined casinos cannot be subdivided. Boss is highest individual die, not highest total or most dice.

operative_quotes: On your own turn you may **build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize and gamble** in **any order**, or stop taking actions. You may repeat actions except **gamble is limited to once per turn**, and **no die may be reorganized more than once per turn**. You must be able to pay the stated action cost. After each action check for boss ties and settle them before continuing.
No player may take an action on another player’s turn. Trading itself is not an action.
answers.answer: Take build, sprawl, remodel, reorganize, and gamble in any order; repeat actions except gamble once and no die reorganized more than once this turn. No one acts on another’s turn.

operative_quotes: Choose **a lot you own**. Take back its marker, choose an **available** casino tile of any color, pay the **price printed on the lot**, and place the tile there. Put one of your dice on it with the **lot’s printed die value** face up. Edge-connected same-color tiles merge immediately; boss control may change.
answers.answer: Build on your $6 lot: take back its marker, choose any available color, pay $6, place tile and die showing 2.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.
answers.answer: Pay $18, place available gold tile with die showing 3 on the empty unowned edge-adjacent lot. Opponent-marked and merely diagonal lots are not legal.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss**. Choose a **new color with enough available tiles for the entire casino**. Pay **$5 per tile** and replace **every tile** of that casino with the new color, returning the old tiles to their supply. Dice stay with their holdings and keep their values. You cannot remodel just part of a casino.

The result merges with any edge-connected casino of the new color. The highest individual die in the resulting casino determines the boss, so a remodel may hand control to another player; settle any cross-player highest tie immediately.
answers.answer: Boss may remodel all two tiles for $10 if two new-color tiles are available. Dice retain values. It merges with connected casinos of that color; highest die controls, so stronger neighbor takes control. Resolve ties immediately.

operative_quotes: You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.

1. Pay **$1 per pip on every die in that casino**, including opponents’ dice, using their values before the roll.
2. **Reroll all dice**, not a chosen subset. Each player rolls their own dice.
3. Each player puts their rerolled dice back on **their own original tiles**. If they have multiple dice, they choose how to assign the rolled values among those tiles; they cannot move onto another player’s former tile. Temporary markers can help remember the original holdings.
answers.answer: Yes. Non-boss with one die qualifies. Acting player pays $10 (5+3+2). All dice reroll, each player rolls their own; results return to owner’s original tiles, with assignment among own multiple tiles permitted.

operative_quotes: You may reorganize different casinos, but **no die can be reorganized twice during the same turn**. A casino containing **any die already reorganized that turn cannot be reorganized**, even after a merger into a larger casino. This limit applies to paid reorganization, **not free boss-tie rerolls**, which happen as often as necessary. Settle boss ties after the action.
answers.answer: No; casino containing a die reorganized earlier this turn cannot be reorganized even after merger. This is a paid-reorganization limit; free tie rerolls remain allowed.

operative_quotes: If **two or more players** tie for the **highest** value in a casino, reroll **all dice currently tied for highest**, **for free**. Leave smaller dice untouched. Reassess the highest value across the whole casino after each roll. If different players still tie for the current highest, reroll the current highest dice again. Continue until only **one player** owns the highest value; several highest dice belonging to that one player need no reroll.

A tie among smaller dice does nothing. If tied bosses roll below a previously smaller die, that unchanged die’s owner becomes boss. For example, Red 5 and Blue 5 reroll to 3 while Green 4 stays: Green becomes boss, without rerolling the 3s further.
answers.answer: Red and Blue reroll tied 5s for free; Green’s 4 stays. If both roll 3, Green’s 4 becomes boss. Highest tie among one player’s dice needs no reroll; lower ties do nothing.

operative_quotes: **Once during your own turn**, choose a casino where **another player is boss**, and give that player the **House card**. If no opponent bosses a casino, you cannot gamble. You may bet no more than **all three limits**: **$5 per tile in that casino**, **your available money**, and **the boss’s available money**.
answers.answer: Limits are $20, $18, and $15; max bet $15. Give House card to opponent boss. Gamble at most once this turn.

operative_quotes:
| Dice sum | Result |
|---|---|
| 3, 4, 9, 10 or 11 | You win: the boss pays you **the bet amount**. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 2 or 12 | You win double: the boss pays you **twice the bet**, limited to the money the boss actually has. You keep/get back your own stake. |
| 5, 6, 7 or 8 | You lose: pay **the bet amount** to the boss. |
answers.answer: At $4: sums 3/4/9/10/11 win $4; sums 2/12 win double but boss can pay only $7; sums 5/6/7/8 lose $4. A winner keeps/gets back their stake.

operative_quotes: Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.

For a transferred lot replace the owner’s marker with the recipient’s marker. For a transferred casino die replace it with the recipient’s die, retaining the **current pip value**, not the board’s printed die. A die trade can therefore change the boss and cause an immediate highest tie.

You **cannot trade points or casino tiles**, or promise actions, exchanges or transfers for **future turns**. **No player can perform an action on another player’s turn.** A current-turn action can be part of a trade only for the player whose turn it is. If something prevents an element of a trade from happening, the subsequent steps of that trade do not occur.
answers.answer: Trade any time except during tie resolution/after end; multiple players may participate. Trade money, lots, dice, active player’s current-turn actions. Replace marker/die, preserve die current value. Points/tiles and future-turn promises barred; no action on another’s turn; failed trade step stops subsequent steps.

operative_quotes: Record casino points by moving your chip on the **printed scoring track**. Numeric gaps are **breaks**: you must earn enough **from that individual casino** to reach the next printed value. Stop before a break you cannot cross and lose unusable excess points; do not save them for later.

When several casinos pay you points on one turn, score them **individually, from smallest to largest**, choosing the order of equal-size casinos. You cannot combine their awards to cross a break. Several separate one-tile casinos therefore still cannot move a chip from 8 to 10.
answers.answer: From 8: 1 leaves 8, 2/3 reaches 10, 4/5 reaches 12. Casinos score individually, smallest first (choose order for equals); no combining separate casinos to cross break.

operative_quotes: As soon as anyone draws **End of Game**, the game ends immediately. Do not take Play actions or initiate trades after that draw. Make the **final payout for all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip**, using normal money, boss-point and scoring-break rules. Highest score after that payout wins. If tied for most points, the tied player with **most money** wins. The source gives no further tiebreak if both remain equal.
In this base game, a player also **wins immediately at 90+ points**.
answers.answer: End draw ends game immediately; no actions/trades. Pay all owned lots and Strip-adjacent casinos normally. High score wins; tie goes to most money, with no further tiebreak stated. 90+ points is an immediate win.

operative_quotes: **Do not build on F block.** During setup, **discard any F-lot card and draw a replacement**; use the two accepted A–E cards for starting lots and money. Discarded F cards remain discarded.

During a turn, an **F-lot card places no marker**, but still causes the normal **owned-lot money and indicated casino money/points**. Discard it in its appropriate pile, then **repeat Draw** until an A, B, C, D or E card has been drawn and resolved. Only then proceed to Play. Thus multiple payouts can happen on one turn; you do not take actions between these draws. **End of Game still ends the game immediately** if drawn during this sequence.
answers.answer: Setup F cards replaced; on turn F places no marker but still pays normally, then repeat Draw until an A–E card resolves before Play. Multiple payouts can occur first.

The limit applies to ownership placement; use any dice for gambling.

- **Money:** the bank’s supply is unlimited. Your money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discard piles. A doubled gambling payout is limited by the boss’s available money, as stated above; action costs must be paid.

1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.
2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.
3. **The indicated casinos pay money and points:** a single-color card pays every casino of that color anywhere on the board. A **Pay The Strip** card instead pays every casino with at least **one edge adjacent to The Strip**, regardless of color. A qualifying casino pays for **all its tiles**, not only the tile touching The Strip.
4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.
5. Discard the property card in its appropriate color/Strip pile so the number already drawn remains countable. Proceed to Play, except that two-player F cards repeat Draw as described below.

If **two or more players** tie for the **highest** value in a casino, reroll **all dice currently tied for highest**, **for free**. Leave smaller dice untouched. Reassess the highest value across the whole casino after each roll. If different players still tie for the current highest, reroll the current highest dice again. Continue until only **one player** owns the highest value; several highest dice belonging to that one player need no reroll.
No actions or initiated trades may interrupt the tie-resolution sequence. These free rerolls do not use up or reset a die’s paid-reorganization allowance.
answers.answer: Resolve immediately on takeover before payouts or Play. It is free, not paid reorganization.

operative_quotes: You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.

1. Pay **$1 per pip on every die in that casino**, including opponents’ dice, using their values before the roll.
2. **Reroll all dice**, not a chosen subset. Each player rolls their own dice.
3. Each player puts their rerolled dice back on **their own original tiles**. If they have multiple dice, they choose how to assign the rolled values among those tiles; they cannot move onto another player’s former tile. Temporary markers can help remember the original holdings.
answers.answer: May reorganize casino where you own all dice; cannot if you own none. Cannot choose only own die: all roll and player pays all pips, including opponents’.

operative_quotes:
- **Casino tiles:** only 9 usable tiles per color. You cannot build or sprawl without the required available tile, or remodel without enough tiles of the chosen new color to replace the whole casino.
- **Ownership dice:** if all 12 of yours are already on the board when you must place one in a casino (including build, sprawl or inheriting a sprawled tile), **remove one of your dice from another tile and use it** at the value required by the new placement. The vacated tile stays, with no owner, and still counts toward its casino’s points. A casino with no dice has no owner/boss. You can trade to free a die. The limit applies to ownership placement; use any dice for gambling.
- **Lot markers:** if all 10 are on the board and you gain a new lot, move one of your markers to it; you cease to own the vacated lot.
- **Money:** the bank’s supply is unlimited. Your money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discard piles. A doubled gambling payout is limited by the boss’s available money, as stated above; action costs must be paid.

**Once during your own turn**, choose a casino where **another player is boss**, and give that player the **House card**. If no opponent bosses a casino, you cannot gamble. You may bet no more than **all three limits**: **$5 per tile in that casino**, **your available money**, and **the boss’s available money**.
answers.answer: No die is removed just to gamble; ownership-die limit does not constrain gambling. Cannot gamble if no opponent bosses a casino.

operative_quotes: You **cannot trade points or casino tiles**, or promise actions, exchanges or transfers for **future turns**. **No player can perform an action on another player’s turn.** A current-turn action can be part of a trade only for the player whose turn it is. If something prevents an element of a trade from happening, the subsequent steps of that trade do not occur.
answers.answer: If reorganization does not make you boss and sprawl cannot happen, subsequent trade steps do not occur. Opponent cannot sprawl on your turn; only active player may perform traded action.

operative_quotes: Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.

As soon as anyone draws **End of Game**, the game ends immediately. Do not take Play actions or initiate trades after that draw. Make the **final payout for all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip**, using normal money, boss-point and scoring-break rules. Highest score after that payout wins. If tied for most points, the tied player with **most money** wins. The source gives no further tiebreak if both remain equal.
answers.answer: No. After End of Game draw, players cannot initiate trade before final payout.

operative_quotes:
- Board with lots grouped in blocks, The Strip, scoring track, wager area and property-card discard spaces.
- **9 usable casino tiles in each of 5 colors:** aqua, brown, gold, purple and silver. A tenth tile of each color is a replacement, not extra supply. Casino colors do not correspond to player colors.
- For each player: **12 dice, 10 translucent lot markers, a scoring chip and an action card**. Player colors are blue, green, red and yellow.
- Money, 49 property cards (including the End of Game card), player card and House card. The deck has **9 cards per casino color and 4 Pay The Strip cards**, including End of Game.

1. Each player takes an action card and all pieces of one player color. Put every scoring chip on **0**. Choose a banker; put money and tiles within reach.
2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.
5. Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.
answers.answer: Each player takes their color’s 12 dice, 10 markers, scoring chip, and action card; chip starts on 0.

operative_quotes: Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.
answers.answer: No; multiple players may participate.

2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.

answers.answer: Choose a banker at setup and put money and tiles within reach.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.
answers.answer: No; must be boss of casino being expanded.

operative_quotes: Choose **a lot you own**. Take back its marker, choose an **available** casino tile of any color, pay the **price printed on the lot**, and place the tile there. Put one of your dice on it with the **lot’s printed die value** face up. Edge-connected same-color tiles merge immediately; boss control may change.
answers.answer: No; Build requires a lot you own, not an unowned or opponent-marked lot.

operative_quotes: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.
answers.answer: No; target must be an empty unowned edge-adjacent lot. Built space is not an empty lot, even with no die.
